workload: Pick the one task that matters most today and let the rest wait.
Look at this week's deadlines and move one low-priority task to a calmer day.
Break your biggest task into three small steps and only start the first.
Try a 25-minute focus block, then a real 5-minute break away from your screen.
If everything feels urgent, write it down. Usually only one or two things truly are.
Ask yourself what can be shortened, not just what can be finished.
rest: Aim for a steady bedtime tonight. Even 30 minutes earlier can help.
Put your phone away 30 minutes before sleep and see how tomorrow feels.
A short walk in daylight can help both energy and sleep.
Drink some water and eat something proper before the next study block.
Schedule one evening this week with no studying at all.
reflect: Write three lines: what was hard today, what went okay, what you need tomorrow.
Name the feeling in one word. Naming it often makes it a little smaller.
Read your last journal entry. What would you say to a friend who wrote it?
Write down one thing you handled better than you expected this week.
mood: Do one small thing today that has nothing to do with deadlines.
Listen to a song you like, all the way through.
Step outside for five minutes and notice three things you can see.
Message someone you feel comfortable with, even just to say hi.
Do something kind for yourself today, however small.
talk: Talking to someone you trust can lighten things. A friend or family member counts.
If it keeps feeling heavy, the university counselling service is there for students like you.
You can use the chat here to talk things through whenever you like.
Telling a lecturer or advisor you are overloaded is allowed, and often helps.
break: Take ten slow breaths: in for four, out for six.
Stand up, stretch your shoulders and look at something far away for a minute.
Take a proper break between tasks. Switching tabs does not count.
Have a short rest before your next study block. You will work better after it.
general: Progress counts even when it is small. Be fair to yourself today.
You do not have to fix everything today.
A rough week does not mean a rough semester.
